claims.text: AddDonHangInfrastructure registers DonHangDbContext with AddDbContext(options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString)), IOrderRepository → EfOrderRepository and INotifier → LoggingNotifier with AddScoped, and returns services.

Program.cs reads ConnectionStrings:Default (throwing if missing), calls AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString), then AddScoped<OrderService>(); it never names EfOrderRepository or LoggingNotifier.

claims.text: AddScoped<TService, TImplementation>() registers TImplementation to be built when TService is requested, with a scoped lifetime; AddScoped<T>() registers T as its own implementation.

In the form Đơn Hàng uses, a C# extension method is a static method in a static class whose first parameter has the this modifier; it can be called with instance-method syntax on that type (C# 14 also adds extension blocks).
UseNpgsql configures the context to use the Npgsql EF Core provider for PostgreSQL with the given connection string.
claims.source_hint: Npgsql EF Core provider docs; examples/don-hang @ stage-1: Directory.Packages.props

claims.text: When a constructor parameter without a default value has no registration, the container throws InvalidOperationException naming the unresolved type; it never fills such a required parameter with null.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: Dependency injection in .NET ('Unable to resolve service for type ... while attempting to activate ...')

claims.text: In the Development environment, WebApplication.CreateBuilder enables ValidateOnBuild, so a registered service with an unresolvable dependency makes builder.Build() throw at startup; Đơn Hàng's docker-compose sets ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development for the api.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Dependency injection (scope validation / ValidateOnBuild in Development); examples/don-hang @ stage-1: docker-compose.yml:93

claims.text: Controllers are not registered in the container by default, so ValidateOnBuild does not check their constructor parameters; a missing registration only a controller needs fails when the controller is activated for a request, and ExceptionHandlingMiddleware turns the exception into 500.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Dependency injection into controllers, AddControllersAsServices; examples/don-hang @ stage-1: ExceptionHandlingMiddleware.cs:26-30

claims.text: One registration serves every constructor that asks for that type; OrdersController and OrderService both receive IOrderRepository from the single AddScoped line.
Keeping infrastructure registrations inside DonHang.Infrastructure means swapping an INotifier implementation changes only that project.
AddDbContext registers the context with a scoped lifetime by default.
